topic: In a timeline where Usopp never joined, nobody was there to burn the World Government flag at Enies Lobby, and the Straw Hats lost one critical advantage
title: Without Sogeking, The Flag Never Burns
description: Luffy turned to his sniper at Enies Lobby and asked him to burn the World Government flag. Sogeking took the shot, declared war on the government in one flame, and changed everything. But what if the sniper who took that shot had never joined the crew?
comment: If Sogeking never burned that flag, does the whole Enies Lobby arc collapse, or do the Straw Hats find another way?

lines.text: At Enies Lobby, Luffy looked at Sogeking and asked for one shot: burn the World Government's flag.

shot.fallback: masked sniper taking aim at a symbol

lines.text: Sogeking did it without hesitation, burned the flag in one perfect shot, and declared war on the entire World Government.
That moment was the crew's declaration: we came here, we fought you, and we didn't just win—we defied you publicly.

shot.fallback: defiant act against a world power

lines.text: But without a sniper on that crew, nobody can take that shot. The flag just keeps flying.
Without that flag burning, Oimo and Kashii never get convinced to switch sides either, because nobody earned their trust on this crew.

shot.fallback: giant guards remaining unfriended and hostile

lines.text: Two guards who should have been allies stay enemies, right when the Straw Hats need every advantage they can find.

shot.search: Two giants fighting against crew cost
shot.fallback: extra enemies on a strained battlefield

lines.text: The whole moment cost them nothing but gained them everything: allies, defiance, a statement heard across the entire world.

shot.fallback: single shot rippling across a world

lines.text: But that was only because one sniper agreed to take an impossible shot that nobody else could make...

shot.search: Sniper impossible shot only he can take
